results.content:
# Trump approval rating slides to new second-term low in latest poll

Portrait of Fernando Cervantes Jr.

After a brief reprieve earlier in the week, President Donald Trump’s approval rating resumed its decline, falling to a new second-term low in the latest Marquette University Law School poll.

The poll, released Tuesday, Sept. 15, found that 37% of Americans approved of Trump’s job performance, down three percentage points from Marquette’s July poll.
results.title: Trump approval rating back on the decline, new poll shows

results.content:
In the latest Reuters/Ipsos poll, Trump’s overall approval fell three points from the previous week to an all-time low of 32 percent. Among Republicans, approval of his job performance dropped from 82 percent to 73 percent in a week, down from 86 percent in January 2026 and 91 percent just after his second inauguration. [...] “Those are striking numbers,” Tyson said. “Numbers that we hadn’t seen until recent weeks here in our Ipsos polling.”

A recent Quinnipiac poll similarly found Trump at his lowest approval to date on the economy, with only 32 percent approving his handling of the issue. Overall, 33 percent approved of his handling of his job, near the 32 percent record notched in July.
results.title: Trump's polls sink further in warning sign for GOP

results.content:
Meanwhile, the latest polling shows Trump with some of the lowest approval ratings he's received.

A Sept. 16-20 American Research Group poll showed just 29% approval and disapproval ratings of 68%. In a Sept. 18-21 Economist/YouGov poll, Trump saw a 62% disapproval rating — and 58% disapproval of his ban on the three networks from the White House. In Michigan, a Sept. 22 Civiqs poll found a 58% disapproval rating of Trump's job performance.
